intendedUse: Allow an internal operations analyst to rely on the tool to draft a structured incident summary from approved ticket fields before the summary is used in the team's internal incident review.
workflowBoundary: Approved incident-ticket fields are supplied; the tool drafts a summary; the summary is checked against the ticket and accepted into the internal review record.
workflowCompletion: The accepted summary matches the defined fields and does not invent unsupported incident facts.
downstreamHandoffs: Follow-up actions remain in the existing incident-management process
movedBottleneck: If drafting becomes faster, verification of source fields and follow-up ownership may become the dominant work.
unhappyPath: If required fields are missing or contradictory, the tool must mark the summary incomplete rather than fill the gap with an invented fact.

actors.role: AI drafting with independent source-field verification

authority: The tool may draft the internal summary only. It cannot close incidents, change production systems, or send external communications.
accountability: The operations team owns the incident record and correction process.
acceptanceCriteria: Every factual statement in the draft is traceable to an approved ticket field.
Missing or contradictory source fields are surfaced rather than silently completed.
The structured output contains the fields required by the internal incident-review template.
knownLimitations: The record establishes the named internal drafting use only; it does not establish autonomous incident resolution.
evidenceRefs: Illustrative acceptance test set: representative completed tickets
Illustrative negative test set: missing and contradictory fields
nextEvidence: If the organisation wants to operate the tool as a standard supported service, establish the Capability gate: ownership, monitoring, recovery, maintenance, support, and operating cost.
stopRule: Withdraw reliance if the representative test set no longer covers the incident types being processed or if unsupported factual statements exceed the agreed tolerance.
